strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck: visual tokens increase the computational burden of the language model. Combining adaptive attention-based selection with key-similarity merging provides a simple reduction module without additional learned parameters.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful accuracy–compression tradeoff across six image benchmarks and two model sizes. At 25% retained tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2 and 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA, while improving ScienceQA from 66.8 to 68.3 (Table 1). These results support the practical contribution.

The training-free Video-LLaVA experiments provide encouraging transfer evidence across three benchmarks. For example, PruMerge improves ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 while substantially reducing tokens (Table 3).

Tables 4–6 provide useful sampling, merging, and fine-tuning ablations. The merging component improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3. Figures explain the pipeline clearly, and the main inherited models, datasets, and token-reduction methods are cited.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not fully establish the contribution beyond combining existing ideas. Table 7 does not specify whether ToMe, ATS, and EViT receive the same additional LoRA fine-tuning as PruMerge+, or sufficiently describe their adaptation to LLaVA. Furthermore, comparison against fixed top-k attention selection at matched average token budgets is missing, so the specific benefit of IQR-based adaptivity remains uncertain.

Practical efficiency is insufficiently validated. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates, with no measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or peak memory. Token-selection and merging overhead, decoding, and batching with variable token counts are not evaluated. Reduced language-model computation is credible, but the magnitude of deployment gains remains unverified, particularly for the better-performing PruMerge+ configuration.

The claimed O(n) clustering complexity in Section 2.2 is not supported by the specified computation. Equation 4 describes an all-token key-similarity matrix, and Algorithm 1 compares each of m retained anchors against the other tokens, requiring O(mn) similarity work at fixed feature dimension. With a fixed retained proportion, this scales quadratically; the claimed asymptotic advantage over CrossGet therefore needs correction or a different implementation.

Several implementation details prevent faithful reproduction from the manuscript. Algorithm 1 doubles the selected token count for PruMerge+, which does not explain the reported change from 5.5% to 25% retention. The neighbor count k is unspecified, and the update is an unnormalized neighbor sum despite the description of weighted averaging. These ambiguities affect both feature construction and the reported operating point.

Performance-preservation claims need narrowing. At 5.5% retention, the 7B model drops from 78.5 to 72.0 on VQAv2, 85.9 to 76.3 on POPE, and 1510.7 to 1350.3 on MME, despite fine-tuning (Table 1). Section 4.1 also incorrectly claims improvement on POPE. These losses do not negate the stronger PruMerge+ tradeoff, but the manuscript should distinguish the two configurations consistently.
